Volume is extremely low right now, and I know why.

For the past couple of days I’ve been posting about the same pattern. Since the hack, Binance futures kept pushing price into liquidation zones while spot buyers quietly absorbed it. Then the pressure slowed. Then it came back. Same exchange, same pattern, same liquidation clusters getting hit again and again.

Now the market has gone quiet. Most market makers are sitting on the sidelines, and the little flow left is still dominated by Binance, with spot buying and futures selling at the same time.

Put it all together and it looks a lot like Binance has used the market to win back what it lost in the hack.
Push price down with futures. Liquidate the longs. Let panic do the rest. Buy the coins people are forced to dump on spot, cheaper. Repeat until the job is done.

And now that volume has dried up, it feels like the job might be close to finished.

I can’t prove it. But I’ve watched this flow every day since the hack, and it hasn’t looked like a normal market once.

When the pressure fully lifts and the other market makers come back, spot will show where price wanted to go all along.

$BTC Did get a big move bit still has not seen a big flush in open interest.

We did see the biggest long liquidation since June when it first broke below $60K.

Funding has also come down considerably due to this, even trading slightly negative as we speak.

With OI still elevated, I do think volatility will remain high, we've been seeing a slow and orderly grind lower for most of this correction and only really seen acceleration the past two days.

A lot of longs were flushed out here ($1.6B+ liquidations the past day alone). So it is safe to assume a lot of that open interest are directional shorts. But many of these positions are just holding from much higher levels and won't be pressured into closing until price at least sees a reasonable bounce.

Of course there's also plenty of longs although the "dip buying" on leverage seems to be somewhat minimal so far the past few hours so that's not bad.

So I do believe there's plenty of fuel but spot first needs to step in and get a reversal going otherwise it's meaningless.

quote.text:
$BTC Open Interest (in BTC) is back at the highest level we've seen since 2021-2023. 

Every time we hit this area during the past year, we saw a flush of open interest soon after. Usually this was due some sort of squeeze in the market which made the open interest top out.

Keep in mind, this says nothing about which direction that squeeze should be in. But in the majority of the other examples on the chart it did cause a reversal in the market instead of further continuation.

This makes sense as positions tend to build up during a trend. Then when that trend reverses you see those positions cover to take profit or get squeezed out. The other side of the trade generally already got washed out multiple times before.
